checks_run: Inspected all 47 submitted regular files, including requirements, starter, public tests, sealed reference material, metadata, license boundary, and submitted validation evidence.
Identified GCC 15.2.0, AArch64 GCC 15.2.1, QEMU 9.1.1, Python 3.11.5, GNU Make 4.2.1, configured GNU Binutils 2.43, and the implicitly selected system GNU ld 2.30 by exact command/path.
Reproduced the candidate structure scan and independently checked archive types, credential signatures, metadata linkage, conservative labels, and sealed placement.
Ran bounded starter compile and public-test targets in a writable copy of the immutable candidate.
Ran a bounded clean hosted reference build, deterministic sequence suite, freestanding AArch64 build, and QEMU boot in the writable copy.
Compiled and ran a reviewer-authored semantic boundary/atomicity suite normally and with AddressSanitizer plus UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.
Compiled and ran a reviewer-authored full-object deterministic-initialization check against the reference RAMFS.
Probed hosted linker selection with and without PATH and with the configured Binutils directory.
Compared the learner and reference headers and verified the original candidate content digest before and after testing.
evidence: Starter compile exited 0; its intentionally incomplete public suite exited 2 with exactly 1/5 checks passing, matching the submitted transcript.
The sealed build exited 0: 7/7 hosted contract groups passed, each subsystem completed 4,000 deterministic operations, the AArch64 ELF had no undefined symbols, and QEMU printed MINIOS: PASS.
The reviewer-authored semantic suite passed process, VM, and filesystem checks both normally and under ASan/UBSan with leak detection disabled.

The deterministic-initialization check failed: on the configured x86_64 ABI sizeof(fs_file_t) is 304 and offsetof(size) is 296; two ramfs_t values prefilled with 0xa5 and 0x5a still differed first at byte 289 after fs_init. Seven padding bytes per file are never cleared by either starter or reference initialization.

The published contract says initializers fully establish deterministic state from arbitrary bytes, while the starter and reference clear only named RAMFS members; existing public and sealed initializer assertions do not inspect padding.

The reference accepts fs_write with data == NULL when count == 0 and the sealed suite requires it, but REQUIREMENTS.md only states that exception explicitly for fs_read, leaving a learner-visible behavioral ambiguity.

A normal hosted link selected /usr/bin/ld 2.30-123.el8, which is absent from toolchain.mk and the submitted tool list. With PATH removed, the absolute GCC command failed because it could not find ld; supplying the configured Binutils 2.43 directory made the link pass.

Independent archive inspection found 18 answer-bearing/reference files and all were under a sealed path; only starter sources and the public test were non-sealed C files. Manifest labels remain GENERATED and PARTIAL with independent validation REQUIRED and productionized false.
The original 47-file candidate aggregate digest was unchanged at f1ac86abff490ab1d3fc20ed45bf5478d61ec536ab398417f3f989e01b79f3d5.
limitations: The immutable upstream snapshot and network were unavailable, so the assertion that no linked upstream material was copied and the upstream license metadata could not be independently compared; only internal provenance consistency was checked.
No actual learner-view projection was provided. Path placement supports progressive disclosure, but end-to-end exclusion of sealed files from a student view was not transfer-verified.
LeakSanitizer cannot run under this workspace's ptrace restrictions; leak detection was disabled for the successful ASan/UBSan run.
No physical Raspberry Pi, independent coverage-guided fuzzing, benchmarking, production assessment, or transfer validation was performed. The candidate honestly makes none of those claims.
This advisory review does not publish or promote a REVIEWED, TESTED, BUILDS, FUZZED, BENCHMARKED, TRANSFER_VERIFIED, or PRODUCTIONIZED label.
